summary.intent: Run GSD's ship-phase loop for phase 77 (crypto-hygiene-and-terminology-canonicalization) autonomously: verify, secure, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit, ship, and resolve PR reviews, triaging every finding per a strict fix/todo/discard rule.
summary.outcome: Completed verify (already passed), secure (State B short-circuit, SECURITY.md authored), and the parallel crypto/privacy + security + simplify review passes; fixed a real key-zeroization gap in registration.ts, a stale comment in encoding.ts, added a locking test, and committed the fixes. Validate, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit, ship, and PR-review resolution steps were still pending at transcript end.

repo: gsd-secure-phase's Step 3 short-circuit rule: if threats_open=0 AND register_authored_at_plan_time=true AND ASVS level==1, skip spawning the gsd-security-auditor entirely and go straight to writing SECURITY.md from the template — only spot-check the highest-severity mitigations manually.

packages/sdk/src/client.ts's sharedFile* codecs are pre-existing from phase 68.2-08 and serve a distinct web↔sdk hex/base64 boundary — folding them into a phase's dedup cleanup is out-of-scope creep even when a simplify pass flags them.
wrap.ts's 1:1 passthrough is a deliberate D-09 seam with test coverage, not dead code — discard simplify findings targeting it.

The zeroization pattern (start `try` immediately after key generation so every post-mint throw path — including early validation throws — zeroes minted keys) lives canonically in file/index.ts; other folder/file registration code should mirror it.

code.finding: TEE-wrap block sat outside the try block; a malformed TEE pubkey throwing in hexToBytes leaked the 3 minted keys. Fixed by moving the try to start right after key generation, matching file/index.ts's pattern, so early validation throws (previously at lines ~88/93) also zero out.

The @cipherbox/crypto test mock omits hexToBytes, bytesToHex, and wrapIpnsKeyForTee — a naive TEE-wrap-throw test fails with an unrelated 'undefined function' error unless those are explicitly mocked.
Contained a stale provenance comment in phase 77's own new file; corrected as part of the simplify pass.

workflow: Launching independent review passes (crypto/privacy review, general security sweep, simplify scan) as parallel background agents while running the GSD write-artifact gates (secure, validate) inline avoids idle wall-clock time.

Don't trust a subagent's specific code claims (e.g. 'client.ts already imports X') at face value — grep/read to verify before acting, since the underlying dedup finding can still be valid even if the agent's supporting detail is wrong.

Behavioral fixes found during security triage (e.g. widening a try block) warrant a purpose-built regression test, not just relying on existing forced-throw tests — check what the mocks actually cover before assuming an existing test would catch a regression.

friction: Simplify-scan subagent asserted client.ts already imported the sharedFile* codecs, which was false per grep — required manual verification before deciding disposition.

folder.test.ts's crypto mock silently omits several functions (hexToBytes, bytesToHex, wrapIpnsKeyForTee) needed for the new zeroization test, requiring extra investigation of imports and mock wiring before the test could be written correctly.
